llm-pretraining.prompt: Approximately how many FLOPs does it take to train a 7-billion-parameter dense model on 2 trillion tokens? Enter the value in units of 102210^{22}1022.
llm-pretraining.explanation: C≈6ND=6⋅7×109⋅2×1012=8.4×1022C\approx6ND=6\cdot7\times10^9\cdot2\times10^{12}=8.4\times10^{22}C≈6ND=6⋅7×109⋅2×1012=8.4×1022.

llm-pretraining.prompt: What did the Chinchilla analysis recommend for a fixed compute budget?
llm-pretraining.explanation: Many models train far beyond that ratio because smaller over-trained models are cheaper to serve.
options: Scale parameters and training tokens together, roughly 20 tokens per parameter
Always use the largest possible model
Train on as few tokens as possible

llm-pretraining.prompt: Which stage first turns a pretrained base model into an instruction follower?
llm-pretraining.explanation: SFT comes after pretraining and before preference tuning or RL.

llm-pretraining.prompt: Thanks to the causal mask, one forward pass over a sequence of T tokens trains on T next-token predictions.
llm-pretraining.explanation: Every position predicts its successor in parallel, which makes LM training efficient.

decoding.prompt: What does a temperature below 1 do to the next-token distribution?
decoding.explanation: Dividing logits by T<1T\lt1T<1 exaggerates their differences.
options: Sharpens it toward the most likely tokens

decoding.prompt: How does top-p (nucleus) sampling choose candidate tokens?
decoding.explanation: The candidate set adapts: small when the model is confident, large when it is not.
options: The smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p
A random subset of size p

decoding.prompt: Which decoding method is a good fit for translation but tends to be bland for open-ended chat?
decoding.explanation: Beam search finds high-likelihood sequences, which favours safe, repetitive text in open-ended generation.

finetuning.prompt: About how many bytes per parameter does mixed-precision Adam training need (weights, gradients, master weights and two moments)?
How many trainable parameters does LoRA with rank 8 add to a single 4096×4096 matrix?
finetuning.explanation: r(d+k)=8⋅(4096+4096)=65,536r(d+k)=8\cdot(4096+4096)=65{,}536r(d+k)=8⋅(4096+4096)=65,536.

finetuning.prompt: Why is LoRA's B\mathbf BB matrix initialized to zero?
finetuning.explanation: BA=0\mathbf B\mathbf A=0BA=0 at the start, so the update begins as a no-op.
options: So the model starts exactly as the pretrained model
Because A\mathbf AA is also zero

finetuning.prompt: Your assistant must answer questions about company policies that change monthly. What is the better first choice?
finetuning.explanation: RAG handles changing knowledge and gives citations; fine-tuning suits style, format and behaviour.
options: Retrieval-augmented generation over the current documents
Train a new model from scratch

alignment.prompt: Why does RLHF add a KL penalty to the reference model?
alignment.explanation: Reward hacking is the main risk when optimizing against a learned reward.
options: To stop the policy from drifting into odd outputs that exploit the reward model
To remove the need for a reward model

alignment.prompt: What does DPO need that standard RLHF also needs?
alignment.explanation: DPO optimizes a classification-style loss directly on preference pairs and a reference model.

alignment.prompt: In GRPO, how is the advantage of each sampled answer computed?
alignment.explanation: Group-relative baselines remove the need for a critic.
options: By normalizing its reward against the mean and standard deviation of rewards in its group

inference.prompt: A model has 32 layers, 8 KV heads of dimension 128, fp16. How many bytes of KV cache per token? (2 for K and V)
inference.explanation: 2⋅32⋅8⋅128⋅2=131,0722\cdot32\cdot8\cdot128\cdot2=131{,}0722⋅32⋅8⋅128⋅2=131,072 bytes, about 128 KB per token.

inference.prompt: Why is generating output tokens memory-bound?
inference.explanation: Batching more sequences raises arithmetic intensity.
options: Each new token requires reading all the weights and the KV cache with little computation per byte
The GPU has too few cores
The prompt is processed one token at a time

inference.prompt: Speculative decoding changes the output distribution of the large model.
inference.explanation: The large model verifies the draft tokens, so the distribution is preserved while latency drops.

inference.prompt: What does a mixture-of-experts layer change?
inference.explanation: A load-balancing loss keeps the experts evenly used.
options: It uses every expert for every token
Each token is routed to a few experts, so total parameters grow while per-token compute stays small

using-llms.prompt: Which practices make LLM outputs more reliable in an application? (select all)
using-llms.explanation: Validation, separation and regression testing are the basics of production prompting.
options: Request JSON matching a schema and validate it in code
Separate instructions from untrusted data with clear delimiters
Maintain an evaluation set and rerun it on every change
Trust outputs because the model sounds confident

using-llms.prompt: LLM-as-judge evaluations have known biases. Which? (select all)
using-llms.explanation: Calibrate judges against human ratings on a sample.
options: Preference for outputs from the same model family

using-llms.prompt: What is the most reliable way to reduce hallucinations about facts?
using-llms.explanation: Retrieved evidence plus verification beats instructions alone.
options: Ground answers in retrieved sources and check citations
Ask the model to be honest

multimodal.prompt: In a LLaVA-style model, what does the projector do?
multimodal.explanation: Projected patch features become "visual tokens" that the language model reads.
options: Maps vision-encoder outputs into the LLM's token embedding space

multimodal.prompt: Which tasks are typical weaknesses of vision-language models? (select all)
multimodal.explanation: Evaluate on your own images, especially for these failure modes.

multimodal.prompt: In the first training stage of a LLaVA-style model, which part is usually trained?
multimodal.explanation: Alignment comes first; instruction tuning later unfreezes more.
options: Only the projector, with the vision encoder and LLM frozen

reasoning.explanation: Majority voting over diverse chains improves accuracy on problems with a single answer.
options: Sampling several reasoning chains and taking the majority answer
Asking the model to agree with itself

reasoning.prompt: What does a process reward model score?
reasoning.explanation: Step-level scores can guide search over reasoning paths.

reasoning.prompt: More test-time compute helps most on tasks with a reliable verifier, such as unit tests or checkable math answers.
reasoning.explanation: Without a verifier, extra samples are hard to choose between.

llm-eval-safety.prompt: From 20 samples with 3 correct, what is the unbiased pass@1 estimate?
llm-eval-safety.explanation: 1−(171)/(201)=1−17/20=0.151-\binom{17}{1}/\binom{20}{1}=1-17/20=0.151−(117​)/(120​)=1−17/20=0.15.
Contaminated scores measure memorization rather than capability.
options: Test items leaked into the model's training data, inflating scores

llm-eval-safety.prompt: What does a sparse autoencoder on model activations try to find?
llm-eval-safety.explanation: Many learned features correspond to human-interpretable concepts.
options: An overcomplete set of sparse, more interpretable features

llm-eval-safety.explanation: Agents that read untrusted content and can act are the main target.
options: Malicious instructions placed in content the model reads, such as a web page or document
A typo in the system prompt

train-small-llm.prompt: With a vocabulary of 16,000 tokens, what should the initial loss be roughly? (natural log, one decimal)
train-small-llm.explanation: A uniform prediction gives ln⁡16000≈9.68\ln16000\approx9.68ln16000≈9.68.

train-small-llm.prompt: Why shift the targets by one position when training a GPT?
train-small-llm.explanation: Inputs are tokens 0..T−1 and targets are tokens 1..T.
options: Each position must predict the next token

train-small-llm.prompt: When instruction-tuning, the loss is usually masked so that it is computed only on…
train-small-llm.explanation: You want the model to learn to produce answers, not to imitate user prompts.

__exam.prompt: A 70B-parameter model is served in 4-bit precision. Roughly how many GB do the weights need?
__exam.explanation: 70×109×0.570\times10^9\times0.570×109×0.5 bytes ≈ 35 GB, plus KV cache and overhead.

__exam.prompt: Which changes reduce KV-cache memory per token? (select all)
__exam.explanation: Memory is proportional to layers × KV heads × head dimension × bytes.
options: Increasing the number of KV heads

__exam.prompt: A fine-tuned model writes in the right style but invents facts about new products. What is the fix?
__exam.explanation: Fine-tuning teaches style; facts that change belong in retrieval.
options: Add retrieval over product documentation and require citations

__exam.prompt: Sorting these by when they occur in a typical LLM's life, which comes last?
__exam.explanation: Tokenizer → pretraining → SFT → preference tuning or RL.

__exam.prompt: Lowering temperature makes a model more knowledgeable.
